requirement_text.REQ-003: Add 'en' to src/i18n/routing.ts's locales array (now ["ru","uz","en"]), defaultLocale stays "ru". Create messages/en.json matching messages/ru.json's 177-leaf-key structure, every value duplicated verbatim from ru.json as a placeholder except Metadata.ogLocale = "en_US". Acceptance criteria: locales array correct; messages/en.json key-set matches ru.json exactly with non-empty values; visiting /en renders <html lang="en"> with /ru and /uz unregressed; LocaleSwitcher renders three working options (RU/UZ/EN) navigating correctly between all three locale prefixes with anchors preserved; npm run build has no type/routing errors; /en renders all landing sections with no missing-translation-key errors.

result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-003, not trusting TEST-RUNNER's report. npm run lint: exit 0, 0 errors, same 4 pre-existing warnings (Avatar.jsx, Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) unrelated to routing.ts/messages/en.json. npm run build: exit 0, compiled successfully, route table shows 'ƒ /[locale]' and 'ƒ Proxy (Middleware)', no type/routing errors. AC1: read src/i18n/routing.ts directly - locales=["ru","uz","en"], defaultLocale="ru", exact match. AC2/AC2b: re-ran my own Node leaf-key-diff and verbatim-value-diff scripts (not the report's copy) against messages/ru.json and messages/en.json - ru_count=177, en_count=177, missing=[], extra=[], empty=[], diff_keys=["Metadata.ogLocale"] with en="en_US"/ru="ru_RU" - matches report exactly. AC3: started my own npm run dev, curled /en, /ru, /uz directly - <html lang> is "en"/"ru"/"uz" respectively; / redirects 307 to /ru; /xx redirects 307 to /ru/xx; /ru/xx returns 404. AC4: curled LocaleSwitcher markup on all three locale pages myself, including /uz which the report never explicitly showed - all three show correct hrefLang/class="on" placement and bare-path hrefs (/ru,/uz,/en) with no hash fragments, consistent across every page checked (anchor preservation follows structurally since next-intl's Link/pathname mechanism is unchanged and hrefs never carry an anchor server-side). Read LocaleSwitcher.tsx directly - confirmed it is fully generic over routing.locales with zero hardcoded locale branches, so this requirement needed no code change there, matching the requirement description's own claim. Read src/i18n/request.ts directly - confirmed it resolves messages by dynamic import keyed on locale with a defaultLocale fallback, needing no change for a third locale, matching the description's claim. AC6: curled /en myself - 0 MISSING_MESSAGE occurrences, only one dotted-string match '>IMPACT.T<' which is a real partner brand name in context, all 10 distinct section ids present (top/about/proof/map/events/streams/team/partners/join/grid), hero content verbatim Russian placeholder as REQ-003 scopes it (translation is REQ-004's job, correctly out of scope here). Confirmed dev server stopped: post-kill curl to :3000 returned status=000 (connection refused). git diff master...HEAD is tightly scoped: only src/i18n/routing.ts (+1/-1) and new messages/en.json touched in application code, no scope creep. docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-003 checked for staleness: status is 'in_progress', which is correct at this pipeline stage (DOC-UPDATER flips to 'done' in Step 6, after this gate) - not stale. Recurring browser-automation-gap MINOR issue (AC4/AC6's literal click-through/theme-toggle steps): confirmed independently via ToolSearch that no Playwright/Puppeteer/browser MCP tool is available in this environment either (only WebFetch matched, which is a read-only markdown-conversion fetcher, not an interactive browser) - the gap is real and still unresolved at this gate too. This is the second consecutive requirement (REQ-001a, now REQ-003) where TEST-RUNNER and RELEASE-VALIDATOR both had to substitute server-rendered/source/CSS evidence for the literal browser-interaction steps in a test spec. Recommend this now be escalated from a per-run MINOR note to a system-level issue (per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md) to provision a browser automation tool - the substituted evidence has been sound both times, but two independent verification stages across two requirements hitting the identical gap is a pattern, not noise, and the equivalent-evidence workaround will not scale indefinitely as more requirements have interactive acceptance criteria.

issues.description: No browser automation tool (Playwright/Puppeteer/browser MCP) is available in this execution environment. AC4's click-through-and-read-document.documentElement.lang steps and AC6's live dark-theme-toggle-and-rescroll steps could not be executed literally; both were substituted with independently-verified server-rendered HTML, source-code, and CSS evidence that supports the same PASS conclusion. Recurred identically at REQ-001a (Step 4, test-reports/report-2026-08-27-WF02-REQ-001a.yaml ISSUE-1) and now at REQ-003 (Step 4 and this Step 5 re-check).
issues.recommendation: Escalate to a system-level issue via docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md to provision a browser automation tool for TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR, since this gap has now recurred across two requirements at two separate pipeline stages each.
